title: Guideline on reliance in medicines regulation

clauses.text: A relying authority keeps full responsibility for its own decisions, even when it uses the assessment of a reference authority.
The relying authority should publish which reference authorities it trusts, the routes that use them, and the conditions each route requires.
When a reference authority changes the approved label or product information, the relying authority should decide within a set time whether to re-review its own approval.
Every change to the patient leaflet, however small, needs a full variation and a new assessment before it is used.
Editorial changes to the patient leaflet, such as punctuation or spacing, that do not alter the meaning may be notified within 30 days without a new assessment.
A change that alters a dose, a warning or a contraindication always needs a full variation before the new leaflet is used.
When the reference authority revises the approved leaflet, the holder must submit the same revision to the Agency within 90 days.
Oral liquids that contain iron, paracetamol or other substances harmful to young children must be supplied in child-resistant packaging.
Child-resistant closures must be tested to a recognised reopenable packaging standard, and the test report must be kept in the quality file.
Medicines that need storage between 2 °C and 8 °C must be transported with a temperature logger in each shipping container.
Any temperature excursion outside the labelled range during transport must be assessed by the qualified person before the batch is released for sale.
A single transport excursion of up to 24 hours below 25 °C may be accepted for cold-chain medicines without a further assessment.
Member authorities should open a re-review within 60 days when a reference authority changes the approved label of a relied-on product.
A marketing authorisation holder must be a pharmaceutical establishment licensed under this law and its executive regulations.
The executive regulations of this law set the procedures for registration, renewal and variation of medicines.
The holder must name a qualified person for pharmacovigilance in the application form, who lives in the country and can be reached at all times.
Each imported vaccine batch must be released by the Agency's laboratory, or by an official control laboratory it recognises, before it is sold.
After a manufacturing site transfer, the existing shelf life may be kept only when stability data from the new site support it.
Feed additives for poultry must list every enzyme on the bag in the national language and give the inclusion rate per tonne.
